title: Grounding a counting round
statement: Fix natural numbers $E,B$, an oracle $\mathcal O:[4]\times\{0,1\}^*\to\{0,1\}$, a Boolean word $x$, a proposition $Q$, and a phase $ph\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$. For every $j\in\mathbb N$ with $j<E+1$ and every counting state $\sigma$ whose register values are all at most $B$, suppose $\sigma.e+2j(if\ ph\ then\sigma.s\ else\sigma.lg)\le B$. If, for every $k'\le B$, the counting procedure started in round state $0$ with phase $ph$, with $e$ increased by $2j(if\ ph\ then\sigma.s\ else\sigma.lg)$ and $k=k'$, terminates on every sequence of choices while keeping every register at most $B$ and accepts exactly when $Q$ holds, then the procedure started in round state $j$ with phase $ph$ and registers $\sigma$ has that same termination, register-bound, and acceptance property.
hypotheses_covered: An oracle on four query types and finite Boolean words
Every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$
For every $k'\le B$, the specified procedure from round state $0$ terminates on every sequence of choices, keeps registers at most $B$, and accepts exactly when $Q$ holds
